notes.note: Both assignment routes answer 201/200 only through the service, and the sweep asserts neither success path: a real write creates a dialer_assignments row whose campaign_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT, so createDisposableCampaign's cleanup would fail. The UI layer's campaign-assign-write spec must own the fixture and delete assignments before the campaign, or the {written, skipped, split} envelope stays unasserted.

mode pass-through is proven only for an invalid value (400 invalid_mode): a route that defaulted an absent mode to 'move' would pass every row and payload test in this layer. The assertion that catches it is the 409 conflicts_require_decision on a conflict-bearing fixture, which belongs to the UI layer's campaign-assign-write spec.

Every refusal that needs state is unasserted at HTTP level: 409 conflicts_require_decision, 409 nothing_to_assign, 409 caller_inactive, 403 caller_not_assignable, 409 campaign_not_assignable and auto-promotion all need a pre-existing assignment row, a caller profile or a non-DRAFT campaign, which this sweep may not create. The routes forward the inputs and return the service error unchanged; the states are the UI layer's campaign-assign-write spec.
